title: the workflow holds when the case gets *ugly*
dek: A deterministic local demonstration of inquiry capture, qualification, proposal drafting, follow-up, CRM output, exception routing, and non-bypassable human approval.

sections.heading: the test verdict
sections.body: All 19 fixture cases produced the expected status and required flags. Every case ended with external sending disabled and HOLD_FOR_HUMAN. This proves local workflow behavior, not integration reliability, client adoption, revenue impact, or market validation.

rows.evidence: The second use of the same lead ID was held and flagged.

rows.claim: Missing, conflicting, sensitive, and low-confidence cases
rows.evidence: Each blocked proposal creation and routed to exception review.
Both were held with explicit flags.
A clean case still returned external_send_permitted=false and HOLD_FOR_HUMAN.

items.title: Tests
items.note: Fixture inspection, duplicate behavior, send blockade.

sections.heading: the green run is not *enough*
sections.body: The receipt was inspected for status, required flags, human hold, and external-send blockade. A live pilot must add connector failure tests, buyer acceptance, operator usability, and observed behavior in approved deidentified cases.
